title: Ah, When Shall I Awake
description: Ah, When Shall I Awake in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 303. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ah, when shall I a-wake From sin's soft sooth-ing power, The slum-ber from my spir-it_ shake, And rise to fall no more! A-wake, no more to sleep, But stand with con-stant care, Look-ing for God my soul to keep, And watch-ing un-to prayer!

lines: The slumber from my spirit shake,
And rise to fall no more!
Looking for God my soul to keep,
But simply to my God display
I know that thou wouldst give.
Thou still art ready to receive
All may obey thy gracious word,
Not one of all the race
But at the throne of sovereign grace
May fall and weep, like me.
And tell thee all my care,
And fill with peace and joy.
And make an end of sin.
Till faith shall make us whole;
Till thou shalt all things new create
Speak, and it shall be done!
Thou shalt the work of faith fulfil,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
